text:
Sam W: Heads-up — I'm drafting a lightweight proposal to smooth ingress queueing for streaming requests so retries don't bulldoze long-lived streams. want quick feedback.
Maya R: SGTM, can you sketch the user-visible behavior first? e.g., deadline preservation vs retry priority?
Sam W: sure. idea: keep per-request deadline, but introduce soft priority buckets that reclaim capacity from low-priority buckets when idle. retries get their own bucket with a token budget that refills slowly.
Kevin L: sounds reasonable. concern: long streams hold slots forever and block retries that could salvage other requests. how do you evict gracefully?
Sam W: eviction policy: prefer preempting best-effort streams that haven't produced tokens in Xs, not active streaming outputs. we can send a soft-cancel (gap trailer) allowing client to resume via resume-token.
Maya R: resume-token flow ties into edge resume design. if we rely on resume tokens, we must ensure tokens are cheap and small (no full KV snapshot).
AJ: +1. also think about the KV cache/tokens interaction — resumed requests shouldn't re-run heavy model compute if prefix in cache. we should add an idempotency key to the resume token.
Kevin L: tradeoff: adding tokens + bookkeeping increases memory. how many simultaneous resume-able sessions do we expect? tens of thousands?
Maya R: empirical: from hosted tests, ~5-10k concurrent long-poll streams per region at peak for some customers. that's manageable if tokens are <1KB and token store is TTL-sharded.
Sam W: implementation sketch: priority_buckets = [latency, default, best_effort, retry_budget]. each bucket has dynamic target concurrency. orphaned streams move to best_effort after inactivity window.
Elaine (infra-bot): note: current edge limiter only exposes global concurrency; will need per-bucket accounting and a new admission hook.
AJ: open question: should retries be allowed to borrow from latency bucket if SLA customer? i.e., route-level affinity for borrowing.
Kevin L: maybe make borrowing policy configurable per-tenant: allow_borrow = [none, only_latency, any]. default: only_latency off for non-enterprise.
Maya R: we also need telemetry — per-bucket wait time, preempt count, resume successes. otherwise we'll tune blind.
Sam W: agree. metrics list so far: bucket_occupancy, preemptions_total, resume_token_issued, resume_token_reused, resume_failures.
AJ: another corner: client deadlines. If a client deadline is reached while waiting in retry bucket, do we surface a fast-fail or attempt a final hedged call?
Kevin L: prefer final hedged call if deadline allows; otherwise fast-fail. but badge clients must be able to opt-out.
Maya R: could be a per-route config: retry_strategy = {budgeted, hedged, none}. budgeted uses token budget; hedged tries one extra immediate attempt.
Sam W: quick config example: ```
route: /v1/stream
concurrency: 200
priority_buckets:
  latency: 50
  default: 100
  best_effort: 30
  retry_budget: 20
retry_policy:
  budget_refill_s: 60
  preempt_inactive_after_s: 20
```
Elaine (infra-bot): reminder: changing refill semantics affects billing/observability; coordinate with billing team if we renormalize units.
AJ: operational playbook: when preemptions spike, degrade best_effort to short-lived cached responses and expand retry_budget temporarily for churny customers.
Maya R: Ops ops: we must ensure preemption doesn't create thundering resume storms — add jitter on resume backoff and a per-tenant resume_rate_limit.
Kevin L: also add a low-overhead fast path for tiny streams (<= N tokens) that bypass bucket locks to reduce tail latency.
Sam W: ok i'll fold these into the draft: per-tenant borrowing flag, resume token idempotency, telemetry, jittered resume backoff, and fast-path for micro-streams. anyone object?
Maya R: no objections. please include a section listing invariants and safety checks (no silent data loss, resume token TTL, backpressure signals).
AJ: thumbs up. can we demo a load test with synthetic long streams + retry storms? results will drive defaults.
Sam W: will run tests this week and post results. planning to send RFC follow-up with config proto + perf numbers.
OpsBot: test-run scheduled: streaming-stress/2024-02-12-12:00 UTC. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/test-results/streaming-stress-20240212
Kevin L: nice. one last nit: include a compatibility note for Dedicated/Private — customers may want to fully disable preemption.
Sam W: good catch. i'll add disable_preemption boolean at the route and tenant level. thanks all :thumbsup:
